source.title: A Comparative Study on the Training Effects of Different Optimizers for Deep Learning Models

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Compares optimizer performance on held-out data in a house-price regression task, extending the optimizer comparison to a task outside the version's image-classification and language benchmarks.
record.gate_note: Table 2 reports test-set MSE and MAE for SGD, Adam, and RMSprop. Convergence speed and training-stability measures are not test-error results. Table 1's header is inconsistent with the surrounding text, so its values are not extracted as accuracy results.
record.test_reason: The study measures held-out error for SGD, Adam and RMSprop in Boston Housing regression, extending V4's optimizer comparison to a new task setting. It is not an original source.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases the conclusion: SGD has the lowest final test errors, Adam converges fastest and has the lowest training-loss variability, and RMSprop is intermediate in convergence speed and stability. Recommendations for non-stationary objectives are interpretations, not results tested here.
record.recipe_differences: Compares SGD, Adam, and RMSprop on one fully connected Boston Housing regression task; uses a single reported learning rate and weight decay setting rather than image-classification or language benchmarks.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper states that learning-rate and batch-size effects were not explored; only one setting is reported for each.
record.peer_reviewed: Journal of Electronics and Information Science, Vol. 10 Num. 2 (2025)
record.problems: Single regression task and small dataset; no uncertainty estimates reported; one fixed set of hyperparameters; no training-error comparison is reported, so the study does not establish whether the test-error differences accompanied equal or better training performance.
record.rows_left_out: Optimizer convergence-time and loss-stability results in Sections 4.1 and 4.3 were left out because they do not measure held-out error.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its coexistence with natural-label generalization.
Width scaling beyond zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image networks and local connectivity.

Image and language benchmarks; optimizer-specific learning-rate or schedule tuning; equal or better adaptive-method training performance; broader tuning; decoupled weight decay; switching optimizers; word-level language models.
Batch-size comparisons and adaptations to large batches.
Dropout effects and interactions with dataset size, augmentation and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, generalization gaps and comparisons with other measures.
Removing memorized examples versus random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: Remove the record's limits_scope verdict: omitted tuning and training-performance comparisons are untested parts, not demonstrated failures. No uncertainty estimates or repeated-run results establish the reliability of the reported differences. The paper acknowledges that its common learning rate may favor SGD. The validation split and actual stopping epochs are unspecified.

versions.untested_parts: Memorization of random labels and natural-label generalization.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.
Image-classification and language benchmarks; broader tuning; training-performance comparison; decoupled weight decay or switching from Adam to SGD; word-level language models.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its association with the generalization gap.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring test accuracy.

relationships.condition: Boston Housing regression with a 13–64–32–1 network, common learning rate 0.001, weight decay 0.001, batch size 32 and early stopping.
relationships.reason: R1–R6 report lower test error for SGD (MSE 2.86, MAE 1.42) than Adam (3.02, 1.51) or RMSprop (3.58, 1.76), supporting the optimizer ordering in this additional setting under fixed hyperparameters.
relationships.display_finding: Reported test MSE and MAE favored SGD over Adam and RMSprop under fixed hyperparameters, but these comparisons remain unverified.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
